test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Many Cubans in circumstances __similar to what I had__ become American citizens at the first opportunity.
solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2: similar to mine"** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The option** "similar to mine" **correctly replaces the underlined segment **"similar to what I had".**
 
• In this context, "similar to mine" refers to circumstances or situations in someone's life that closely resemble or are equivalent to the speaker's own experiences or situations.
 
• The phrase "similar to mine" agrees in grammar reference and level of formality with the rest of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is ***"similar to mine".***

**Corrected Sentence:** *Many Cubans in circumstances **similar to mine__** had become American citizens at the first opportunity.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's check why the other options are not correct:
 
 
• Options including "those of mine" and "that of mine" are ungrammatical in this context.
 
• The option "similar to what I have" might be grammatically correct, but it subtly changes the meaning of the sentence, implying ongoing circumstances, whereas the original sentence refers to past circumstances.
